items.title: A closed subscheme whose fibres are Cartier divisors is locally contained in a relative effective Cartier divisor, and agrees with one under flatness or local principality
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a flat morphism locally of finite presentation a closed subscheme whose fibre at a point is a Cartier divisor is locally contained in a relative effective Cartier divisor agreeing with it on that fibre, with equality under a flatness or a local principality hypothesis, and it derives the corresponding global criteria (statement lines 4190-4213). The counted proof is a substantial local argument with genuinely different layers: it reduces to affine rings and to a single local equation on the fibre, spreads the situation out to a Noetherian model by the flat finite presentation approximation, uses Grothendieck's statement and the neighbourhood theorem for regular elements together with the openness of flatness to make the model's equation a relative effective Cartier divisor, base changes back, and then upgrades containment to equality by the isomorphism criterion for flat local algebras and by comparing local equations, finally deducing the global criteria (proof lines 4215-4291). It is H2: the argument is fully carried out in the counted span and its inputs are standard algebra theorems of the openness and approximation type.
